title: oncall-context-condenser-and-active-failure-prober
author: Leo Park
description: Motivation: oncall responders are overloaded with noisy context during incidents and often lack a safe, automated way to exercise likely failure modes against live stacks for faster triage. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a compact oncall context condenser that produces a sanitized, prioritized brief for the active responder, and an Active Failure Prober: a controlled synthetic probe runner that executes low-impact health checks and dependency sanity tests with safety gates and dry-run modes. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-first-action by surfacing the highest-confidence context and remediation hints; 2) enable safe, automated probes that can validate hypotheses without escalating blast radius; 3) provide observability hooks so every probe is tied to an incident ID and reversible. Changes include: new condenser engine (pkg/condenser) using weighted telemetry heuristics + fuzzy dedupe; probe orchestrator (pkg/prober) with policy-driven safety checks, rate limits, and canary targets; Slack and PagerDuty response templates that include condensed brief and probe runbook links; CLI extension for ops to trigger dry-run probes locally; integration tests and a small e2e harness. Checklist: - [x] condenser core implemented and unit tested - [x] prober orchestrator with safety policy engine and timeouts - [x] Slack responder attachment and brief link - [x] dry-run CLI mode and documentation - [x] CI tests and small-scale e2e simulation - [x] security review for K8s exec and network probes How this is intended to be used: incident-bot will append a condensed brief to the incident thread when an alert is created or on-demand via /brief; responders can optionally trigger the Active Failure Prober using the brief UI which runs only allowed probes (as configured per team) and returns structured results in the thread. Safety model: by default probes are dry-run and only run active checks if the incident severity is P0 and an approver label is present; all probes are logged, reversible where possible, and can be disabled via feature flags. Related work: builds on ENG-2156 (telemetry prioritization) and the prior incident-bot snapshotter PRs. Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident-bot.feature.condenser and prober feature flags with a controlled 10% rollout to SRE teams, monitor error-budget impact and false-positive probe runs for 2 weeks, then expand.
commits: feat(condenser): add condensed-brief generator with prioritization weights
feat(prober): initial probe orchestrator, safety policy and dry-run mode
docs: add runbook and devguide for prober usage and security rationale
ci_checks: security-scan: pass with note about K8s exec usage
review_comments: Aisha: Please add a clearer opt-out mechanism for teams that don’t want probes enabled. Reply: Added team-level feature flag and CLI opt-out flag.
Marco: The policy engine needs a max-duration safeguard per probe. Reply: Added per-probe timeout and global orchestrator hard cap.
Riley: Can we avoid storing sensitive telemetry in condensed briefs? Reply: Condenser now runs a sanitizer and redaction pass and records only abstracted hints.
merge_summary: Squashed 3 commits into feature commit; updated docs and added tests. Rollout feature flags set for canary.
release_notes: Added oncall context condenser to produce concise incident briefs and an Active Failure Prober for safe, policy-driven synthetic checks. Feature behind flags with limited SRE canary. See docs/runbooks/oncall_condenser_and_prober.md for usage and security considerations.
